title: Execution equals transcript output
statement: Let $X$, $Y$, and $\alpha$ be types, let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol with inputs in $X$ and $Y$ and outputs in $\alpha$, and let $(x,y)\in X\times Y$. Running $p$ on $(x,y)$ gives the same value as reading the output attached to the transcript produced by that execution.
hypotheses_covered: A protocol $p$ over input types $X,Y$ and output type $\alpha$
replaced:
Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice)
and $Y$ (Bob) with output type $\alpha$, and let $(x, y) \in X \times Y$ be an input
pair. Running $p$ on $x$ and $y$ produces the same value as first executing $p$ on
$(x,y)$ to obtain its syntactic transcript and then reading off the output value
attached to the leaf of that transcript.
